# Adjudication Task — Chapter 344

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃344화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- 연계 퀘스트, [만독지환(萬毒指環)]이 생성되었습니다!
 10|
 11|- 반드시 해내야 하는 일, 당신은 거부할 수 없습니다!
 12|
 13|
 14|
 15|나는 시스템 알림과 동시에 눈앞을 가득 채우는 홀로그램 창을 바라봤다.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|퀘스트
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|[만독지환(萬毒指環)]
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|천하의 그 어떤 독도 흡수한다는 만독지환은 사천당문의 신물이자 무림에 내려오는 전설 중 하나입니다.
 28|
 29|소유자도, 실존 여부도 확실치 않으나 현재로서는 그것만이 유일한 해법입니다!
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|등급 : 절정
 34|
 35|제한 : 진태경
 36|
 37|임무 : [만독지환] 획득 (미완료)
 38|
 39|보상 : 대량의 경험치
 40|
 41|실패 : 적천강의 죽음
 42|
 43|
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|“어떤 독도 흡수한다는 신물이라.”
 48|
 49|내 중얼거림에 문경이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 50|
 51|“맞습니다. 그게 만독지환이 가진 효능이지요. 다만 한 가지 문제가 있는데…….”
 52|
 53|“소유자도, 실존 여부도 불분명하다는 거겠지.”
 54|
 55|“예, 심지어 사천당문에서도 만독지환의 존재를 여러 차례 부정한 적이 있습니다.”
 56|
 57|신의가 무거운 목소리로 덧붙였다.
 58|
 59|“그래서 전설인 게지. 너무 오래되어 사람들의 입을 통해서만 전해져 내려오는.”
 60|
 61|잠시 생각에 잠겼던 내가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 62|
 63|“아뇨. 있습니다.”
 64|
 65|“음?”
 66|
 67|“만독지환은 분명히 존재합니다. 단지 감춰져 있을 뿐이에요.”
 68|
 69|“어찌 그리 확신하시오?”
 70|
 71|신의는 물론이고, 처음 만독지환에 관한 이야기를 꺼낸 문경까지 눈을 동그랗게 뜨고 날 바라본다.
 72|
 73|“그거야 당연히…….”
 74|
 75|시스템 때문이지.
 76|
 77|이건 적천강의 치료를 위한 연계 퀘스트다.
 78|
 79|만독지환이 정말 존재하지 않는 물건이라면, 지금 같은 퀘스트도 생성되지 않았을 것이다.
 80|
 81|물론 이 자리에서 그런 말을 했다간 정신병자 취급받기 딱 좋겠지.
 82|
 83|나는 자연스럽게 말을 이었다.
 84|
 85|“그런 신물이 있다고 하면 사람들이 가만히 있겠습니까. 사천당문은 무림에서도 외골수로 유명한데, 당연히 귀찮은 일은 피하고 싶었겠죠.”
 86|
 87|동전 한 푼, 만두 하나로 살인이 벌어지는 세상이다. 하물며 만독지환 같은 신물이라면 얼마나 많은 날 파리들이 꼬일 것인가.
 88|
 89|대충 둘러댄 말이지만 설득력 있는 추론에 사람들이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 90|
 91|“일리가 있는 말이야. 사실 본 방에서도 만독지환의 실존 여부에 대하여 많은 조사를 해 본 결과…….”
 92|
 93|나는 기다렸다는 듯이 입을 여는 궁기방을 바라봤다.
 94|
 95|“됐고. 뒷이야기는 여기 남아서 무진이한테나 해 줘라.”
 96|
 97|“응? 남아? 혁무진이랑 여기 남아 있으라고?”
 98|
 99|“조장님, 그게 무슨 말씀이세요?”
100|
101|“무슨 말씀이긴. 들은 그대로지.”
102|
103|나는 어안이 벙벙한 두 녀석을 차례대로 가리켰다.
104|
105|“혁무진, 궁기방은 여기 남는다.”
106|
107|“왜! 어째서!”
108|
109|“저도 같이 가고 싶습니다! 제발 이 포악한 거지와 저를 남겨 두지 마세요!”
110|
111|“뭐라! 이런 개뼉다구 같은 놈이!”
112|
113|빡! 빡!
114|
115|역시 이럴 때는 매가 약이다. 나는 동시에 정수리를 감싸 쥐는 녀석들에게 주먹을 흔들어 보였다.
116|
117|“헛소리하지 말고 남아서 묘령사태나 지키고 있어. 혹시 무슨 일 생기면 궁기방, 네가 바로바로 연락하고.”
118|
119|“연락? 여기에 사천당문으로 가는 전서구가 있나?”
120|
121|“뭔 거지발싸개 같은 소리 하고 있어. 일 생기면 발바닥에 불이 나도록 뛰어와야지.”
122|
123|“그게 무슨!”
124|
125|“싫으면 하나 길들이든가. 저기 꽃밭에 나비 많더라.”
126|
127|비록 짧은 시간이었지만 냉정한 분석 끝에 나온 결론이다.
128|
129|우선 무공, 특히 신법이 가장 뒤떨어지는 혁무진을 남기고 혹시 모를 대책으로 궁기방을 붙여 놓는다.
130|
131|나름 쓸 만한 절정 고수인 데다, 눈치만큼이나 발이 빠른 녀석이니 혹시 모를 사태에 대비할 수 있을 것이다.
132|
133|“내 결정에 불만이 있거나 궁금한 점이 있다. 즉시 거수.”
134|
135|“……그 주먹이나 내려놓고 물어봐라.”
136|
137|“……전 그냥 여기 남아 있겠습니다.”
138|
139|그때, 한 사람의 팔이 번쩍 치켜 올라갔다. 청풍이 천진난만한 얼굴로 물었다.
140|
141|“은인, 저는요?”
142|
143|“청 소협은 나랑 같이 사천당문으로 가는 거지.”
144|
145|“왜요?”
146|
147|“남겨 놓으면 뭔 사고를 칠 줄 알고. 당신은 촌각이라도 내 시야에서 벗어나지 마. 알겠어?”
148|
149|“네에…….”
150|
151|풀죽은 청풍의 대답에 신의가 안쓰러운 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
152|
153|“너무 뭐라 하지 마시구려. 순진한 청년 같아 보이는데.”
154|
155|“순진하죠. 산불 내서 여기 홀랑 다 태워 버릴 만큼.”
156|
157|“허허, 설마하니 그러겠소.”
158|
159|“며칠 안에 초가삼간 다 태워 먹고, 집 잃은 동 노인께서 개방 입문 한다에 무진이 왼쪽 손목 걸겠습니다.”
160|
161|“……!”
162|
163|청풍을 경계 어린 표정으로 훑어본 신의가 대답했다.
164|
165|“함께 가는 게 좋겠구려.”
166|
167|“현명한 선택이십니다.”
168|
169|“경아, 너는 어찌 하겠느냐?”
170|
171|뭔가를 곰곰이 생각하던 문경도 결심한 듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
172|
173|“저도 스승님을 따르겠습니다. 아미파의 여스님은 휴식만 취하면 아무런 문제도 없을 테니까요.”
174|
175|“그래 주면 고맙고.”
176|
177|사실 지금 내가 가장 필요로 하는 사람은 신의다. 하지만 늘 스승의 곁에서 조수 역할을 톡톡히 해 주는 문경이 있다면 더더욱 좋다.
178|
179|애초에 만독지환에 관한 이야기를 처음 꺼낸 것도 녀석이고.
180|
181|‘남은 건 만독지환을 어떻게 얻어 내느냐는 건데.’
182|
183|만독수라 당사독. 사천당문의 주인인 그와 대면한다면 확실히 알게 될 것이다.
184|
185|생각을 끝마친 나는 청풍을 향해 입을 열었다.
186|
187|“청 소협, 지게랑 밧줄 두 개씩 챙겨. 크고 튼튼한 걸로.”
188|
189|“은인, 지게와 밧줄은 왜요?”
190|
191|“최대한 빠르게 가야지. 가다가 떨어트리면 큰일 나니까 밧줄로 꽁꽁 묶고.”
192|
193|내 말을 들은 신의와 문경의 얼굴이 새하얗게 물들었다.
194|
195|
196|
197|* * *
198|
199|
200|
201|어두운 대전(大殿). 노인의 입이 열린 것은 중년인이 들어오고 나서도 한참 후였다.
202|
203|“오십여 년 전, 네가 태어나기도 전에 본가는 큰 수모를 겪어야 했다. 알고 있느냐?”
204|
205|노인, 만독수라 당사독의 말에 중년인이 고개를 숙였다.
206|
207|“어찌 모르겠습니까.”
208|
209|“당시 약관이었던 노부는 그 모든 것을 똑똑히 지켜보았다. 사방에서 가솔들이 죽어 나가고, 병기창은 불탔으며 전각은 무너졌지. 우리는 그렇게 패자가 되어 사천에서 물러나야 했다.”
210|
211|그렇게 장장 십 년간 이어진 대전쟁은 정파의 승리로 막을 내렸고, 당문은 사천으로 돌아와 가문을 재건했지만 그때의 상처는 모두의 가슴 깊숙이 새겨졌다.
212|
213|“한데, 한데 어찌하여!”
214|
215|당사독의 두 눈동자에 녹색 광채가 번뜩인 순간, 그의 전신으로부터 흘러나오는 독기(毒氣)에 중년인이 숨을 삼켰다.
216|
217|“흡.”
218|
219|“어찌하여 또 다시 이런 수모를 겪을 수 있단 말이냐!”
220|
221|치이이익!
222|
223|자글자글 주름 잡힌 손이 탁자를 짚었다, 아니, 녹였다.
224|
225|나무는 물론이고 모서리에 장식한 철까지 새카만 독액이 되어 흐르는 광경에 중년인이 부복했다.
226|
227|“고정하십시오, 가주님!”
228|
229|중년인의 만류에도 당사독의 분노는 쉬이 가라앉지 않았다.
230|
231|지금 그가 보이는 분노는 당연한 것이었다. 아버지인 독왕 당사문을 해친 흉수를 찾기는커녕, 헛물만 켠 끝에 청성파의 급보를 받고 돌아와야 했으니까.
232|
233|“감히 어느 놈이……!”
234|
235|청성파가 보낸 전서의 내용은 짧았다. 그리고 독왕의 죽음만큼이나 충격적이었다.
236|
237|‘단신으로 아미파의 경천신니와 세 장로를 모두 죽이다니.’
238|
239|그것도 개인을 노린 암습이 아닌, 정면 승부였다고 했다.
240|
241|경천신니는 십왕(十王)의 말석이나마 노려볼 수 있는 초절정 고수. 함께 동석하고 있던 세 장로 역시 경륜 있는 절정 고수들이었다.
242|
243|흉수는 일파의 수뇌부를 홀로 쓰러트린 뒤 유령처럼 사라진 것이다.
244|
245|‘그 정도의 고수가 둘일 리는 없다. 필시 아버님을 해한 것도 그놈이 분명해.’
246|
247|서서히 가라앉는 분노의 빈자리를 채운 것은 경계심이었다.
248|
249|그는 아들이 아닌 사천당문의 가주로서 귀환을 결정했고, 한편으로는 흉수를 추적하는 것 또한 잊지 않았다.
250|
251|“녹영대(綠影隊)는 어찌 되었느냐?”
252|
253|“다섯 명씩 열 개 조로 나누어 성도를 중심으로 청성, 아미, 익산, 삼합 등으로 흩어져 임무를 수행하고 있습니다.”
254|
255|녹영대는 사천당문 내부에서도 첩보와 요인암살에 특화된 이들.
256|
257|정마대전 직후 수많은 마두들을 척결할 수 있었던 일등 공신이었지만, 당사독은 왠지 모를 불길함을 느꼈다.
258|
259|“방심해서는 안 된다. 수문각 방비를 철저히 하고 그 누구의 출입도 허락해서는 안 될 것이다.”
260|
261|“예.”
262|
263|“이만 나가 보아라.”
264|
265|조심스럽게 돌아서는 중년인을 바라보던 당사독이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
266|
267|“이번 일만 끝나면…… 수문각주는 다른 이에게 넘기고 내당(內堂)으로 자리를 옮기거라.”
268|
269|“가, 가주님?”
270|
271|“가주가 아니라 숙부로서 하는 말이다. 네 나이도 곧 지천명을 바라보는데, 하나뿐인 조카를 언제까지 수문각에 남겨 둘 줄 알았더냐?”
272|
273|“가, 감사합니다. 숙부님.”
274|
275|당사독은 소매를 펄럭이는 것으로 대답을 대신했다.
276|
277|잘나지도 않았지만, 딱히 못난 구석도 없는 조카다.
278|
279|세월에 무뎌져 오랫동안 잊고 살았건만…… 정마대전 도중 목숨을 잃은 형님이 생각난 것은 최근의 일이다.
280|
281|“저도 늙은 모양입니다. 아버지.”
282|
283|홀로 남은 당사독의 작은 독백에, 그의 가슴께가 들썩이더니 뭔가가 스르륵 고개를 내밀었다.
284|
285|쉬쉭. 쉭.
286|
287|눈처럼 새하얀 몸통과 푸른 눈. 세모꼴의 머리에 두 개의 뿔이 달린 그것은 한 마리의 뱀이었다.
288|
289|무림에는 천년독각사(千年毒角蛇)라는 이름으로 알려진 영물이자 포악하기로 악명 높은 그것은 길쭉한 혀를 내밀어 당사독의 뺨을 핥았다.
290|
291|“녀석…….”
292|
293|딱딱하게 굳어 있던 당사독의 얼굴이 스르륵 풀어졌다.
294|
295|신경질적인 성격에 사람 만나기를 싫어하는 그였지만, 이 천년독각사에게만큼은 예외였다.
296|
297|아버지인 독왕에게 처음이자 마지막으로 받은 선물. 자식이 없는 그에게는 무엇보다 애틋한 존재였다.
298|
299|“어허, 간지럽다. 인석아.”
300|
301|희미하게 웃으며 뱀의 재롱을 바라보던 그때, 점점 가까워지는 누군가의 발걸음 소리에 새하얀 몸통이 황급히 당사독의 품 안으로 쏙 들어갔다.
302|
303|“무슨 일이냐?”
304|
305|“가주님, 접니다.”
306|

The Divine Physician’s and Mungyeong’s faces turned deathly pale.

[P77]
* * *

[P78]
The dark main hall was silent. Even after the middle-aged man entered, it was a long while before the old man finally opened his mouth.

[P79]
“More than fifty years ago, before you were even born, our family suffered a great humiliation. Do you know about it?”

[P80]
At the Myriad-Poison Asura Tang Sadok’s words, the middle-aged man lowered his head.

[P81]
“How could I not?”

[P82]
“This old man was barely twenty at the time, and I witnessed it all with my own eyes. Our people died all around us, the armory burned, and the pavilions collapsed. We were defeated and forced to withdraw from Sichuan.”

[P83]
The Great Faction War raged for ten long years before ending in victory for the orthodox faction. The Tang Clan returned to Sichuan and rebuilt, but the scars from that time had been carved deep into everyone’s hearts.

[P84]
“And yet… And yet, how?”

[P85]
Green light flashed in Tang Sadok’s eyes. As toxic energy poured from his entire body, the middle-aged man sucked in a breath.

[P86]
“Hngh.”

[P87]
“How can we suffer such humiliation again?”

[P88]
Sssssss!

[P89]
Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand pressed down on the table—or rather, melted it.

[P90]
Not only the wood but even the iron fittings along its corners liquefied into black poison. The middle-aged man immediately prostrated himself.

[P91]
“Please calm yourself, Family Head!”

[P92]
Despite the middle-aged man’s plea, Tang Sadok’s anger did not easily subside.

[P93]
His fury was only natural. Instead of finding the culprit who had harmed his father, Poison King Tang Taesang, he had come up empty and been forced to return after receiving an urgent message from the Qingcheng Sect.

[P94]
“How dare they…!”

[P95]
The message sent by the Qingcheng Sect had been brief. It had also been as shocking as the Poison King’s death.

[P96]
*He killed Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun and three Emei Elders all by himself.*

[P97]
And it had not been a surprise attack targeting a single person. It was said to have been a head-on fight.

[P98]
Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun was a Supreme Peak master who could have vied for even the lowest seat among the Ten Kings. The three Elders with her were also seasoned Peak masters.

[P99]
The culprit had single-handedly brought down the leadership of an entire sect, then vanished like a ghost.

[P100]
*There can’t be two masters of that level. It must have been the same bastard who harmed Father.*

[P101]
As his anger slowly subsided, wariness took its place.

[P102]
He had decided to return not as a son but as the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. At the same time, he had not forgotten to pursue the culprit.

[P103]
“What became of the Green Shadow Squad?”

[P104]
“They divided into ten groups of five and scattered from Chengdu toward Qingcheng, Emei, Yishan, Sanhe, and the surrounding areas to carry out their missions.”

[P105]
Even within the Sichuan Tang Clan, the Green Shadow Squad specialized in intelligence gathering and assassinating key targets.

[P106]
They had played the greatest role in eliminating countless fiends after the Great Faction War, yet Tang Sadok felt an inexplicable sense of foreboding.

[P107]
“Do not let your guard down. Strengthen the defenses of the Gate Guard Pavilion, and do not allow anyone to enter.”

[P108]
“Yes.”

[P109]
“You may leave.”

[P110]
Tang Sadok watched the middle-aged man turn away cautiously, then suddenly spoke.

[P111]
“Once this matter is over… hand the position of Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion to someone else and move to the Inner Hall.”

[P112]
“F-Family Head?”

[P113]
“I’m saying this as your uncle, not as the Family Head. You’re nearly fifty. How long did you think I would leave my only nephew at the Gate Guard Pavilion?”

[P114]
“Th-Thank you, Uncle.”

[P115]
Tang Sadok answered with a flick of his sleeve.

[P116]
His nephew was not exceptional, but neither was there anything particularly lacking in him.

[P117]
Tang Sadok had grown numb with time and lived for many years without thinking about it. Only recently had he begun remembering his elder brother, who had lost his life during the Great Faction War.

[P118]
“I suppose I’m growing old too, Father.”

[P119]
At Tang Sadok’s quiet monologue, something stirred at his chest and slowly poked its head out.

[P120]
Hiss. Hiss.

[P121]
It had a body as white as snow, blue eyes, and a triangular head crowned with two horns. It was a snake.

[P122]
A spiritual creature known throughout the Murim as the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, it was notorious for its ferocity. It flicked out its long tongue and licked Tang Sadok’s cheek.

[P123]
“You little rascal…”

[P124]
Tang Sadok’s stiff expression slowly softened.

[P125]
He had a prickly personality and disliked meeting people, but he made an exception for this Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake.

[P126]
It was the first and last gift he had ever received from his father, the Poison King. Since Tang Sadok had no children of his own, the snake was more precious to him than anything.

[P127]
“Hey, that tickles. You little thing.”

[P128]
He was watching the snake’s antics with a faint smile when the sound of approaching footsteps grew louder.

[P129]
The white body hurriedly slipped back inside Tang Sadok’s robes.

[P130]
“What is it?”

[P131]
“Family Head, it’s me.”

[P132]
At the voice of his nephew, who had left only moments earlier, Tang Sadok affected a frown.

[P133]
“Why have you come back?”

[P134]
“Well, those people have come again.”

[P135]
“Those people?”

[P136]
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi Jin Taekyung and Huashan Divine Dragon Cheongpung.”

[P137]
“I explicitly ordered that no one be allowed inside. Refuse them entry.”

[P138]
“But… one of them may be the Divine Physician.”

[P139]
“What? The Divine Physician?”

[P140]
For once, even Tang Sadok could not hide his surprise.

[P141]
*Who was the Divine Physician? A man said to have reached the divine realm through his medical arts. A mysterious figure who had not shown himself for many long years.*

[P142]
*Why had that very Divine Physician come to our family?*

[P143]
His hesitation did not last long. A hoarse voice escaped Tang Sadok’s lips.

[P144]
“Let them in.”

[P145]
* * *

[P146]
“Are you the Divine Physician?”

[P147]
Now there was a macho man with no brakes.

[P148]
Tang Sadok asked without so much as looking at us, and the Divine Physician let out a hearty laugh.

[P149]
“This old man’s name is Dong Feng.”

[P150]
“Then you are not the Divine Physician?”

[P151]
“People have given this old man an undeserved name.”

[P152]
“Seems you are, then.”

[P153]
“You believe me rather easily.”

[P154]
“Unless someone is desperate to die, no one tells lies in front of this old man.”

[P155]
“……”

[P156]
That was pretty damn convincing.

[P157]
Tang Sadok slowly looked us over, a green glow shimmering in his eyes.

[P158]
“The Divine Physician… You vanished without a trace while the whole world searched for you, yet now you have come looking for me. And with young prodigies of the Murim, no less. Why?”

[P159]
“May I answer that?”

[P160]
I stepped forward, and Tang Sadok’s gaze collided with mine in midair.

[P161]
“Go ahead. If you say something nonsensical, be prepared to become a handful of blood…”

[P162]
“Please lend me the Myriad-Poison Ring.”

[P163]
At my own macho-man-with-no-brakes delivery, Tang Sadok’s pupils trembled.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
